detail.name: WolfgangHUD
detail.desc:
This is a Mod collection of several useful HUD altering mods and a few gameplay tweaks.
Based on [WolfHUD](https://modworkshop.net/mod/15901) by Kamikaze94, rewritten for RAID WW2 as WolfgangHUD.

Requirements:
- [RAID-SuperBLT](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49744) (base 2.4.0 or newer)
- [WaypointsLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/52686)

BeardLib is not required.


## Included mods / features

 * [Kick a Friend](https://modworkshop.net/mod/15175) made by **FishTaco**
 * [HUD Lists](https://bitbucket.org/pjal3urb/hudlist/src/) originally made by **Seven**, modified by **Kamikaze94** in [WolfHUD](https://modworkshop.net/mod/15901), rewritten to RAIDWW2
 * [KillCounter](https://bitbucket.org/pjal3urb/customhud/src) made by **Seven**, modified by **Kamikaze94**, ported to RAIDWW2
 * [Accuracy Plugin](https://bitbucket.org/pjal3urb/customhud/src) made by **Seven**, ported to RAIDWW2
 * [Floating Health Bars](https://modworkshop.net/mod/20330) originally made by **Zenyr** for [PocoHud](https://steamcommunity.com/groups/pocomods), made standalone and then ported to RAIDWW2
 * Interaction lock & timer, reload & melee charge indicator rewritten for RAIDWW2 , based on WolfHUD's implementation, which was basically made by **Seven**, **Kamikaze94**. There are several others out there, you may know it as Push2Interact or Press2Hold etc.
 * DamagePopups made by **Kamikaze94** for WolfHUD
 * NoSlowMotion made by **Kamikaze94** for WolfHUD (i think)
 * InstantRestart made by **Kamikaze94** for WolfHUD (i think)
 * RestartHotkey
 * AutoReload
 * ReadyUpOnNumEnter
 * RealisticReload (drops leftover bullets in magazine)
 * FOVBasedSensivity ported from PD2 (originally by Frankelstner)
 * Suspicion HUD ported from PD2
 * optional PD2 Style HUD Layout
 * End stats
 * Down/Revive Counter
 * HiddenStats
 * ForceReady
 * ChatTweaks
 * SkipIntro/StraightToMainMenu
 * StealthableMissions
 * LoadingStatus
 * Player Pings
 * NoToastSound

Pretty much all features are optional, and can be configured in game.



Big credit goes to all of you!
Without your awesome mods, I would not even have started playing this game at all.
**If I forgot to mention you, I'm really sorry. Please feel free to contact me, so I can credit you, for the awesome stuff you have made :)**


## Recommended Mods to use with WolfgangHUD:

##### no BeardLib required:
[3DPings](https://modworkshop.net/mod/52713) Configurable, network-shared 3D Pings with multiple icons and an action wheel, like the comms wheel.

[AssaultInfoRAID](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59729) shows what the assault AI is doing (phase, time left, enemies alive) in a small info box.

[Better BAR](https://modworkshop.net/mod/47659) Removes the rear sight on the bar for better visibility.
[Better categories in weapon selection menu](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49176) Categories like "SMG", "Shotgun", "Sniper", etc. instead of just "All" and "Equipable".
[Better Server Browser](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50230) Removes the 'friend-only' option and just lists both at the same time (public and friends-only).
[Bots Have Feelings - Reborn](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50170) Improvements for the team-mate bots.
[BountyGrinder](https://modworkshop.net/mod/52537) Let's you freely grind the current daily bounty, even if already completed.
[BountyHunter](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59727) adds a custom bounty with a seed of your choice to the raid selection.
[CampFixes](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59856) repairs unfinished camp logic (toilet break, golden bomb banter, ...).
[Debriefing Cutoff Fix](https://modworkshop.net/mod/43204) lets you actually watch every second of the debriefing videos.
[Drop all bags keybind](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49360) Custom keybind to drop all bags so you don't have to hold G and go through the selection UI.
[Enhanced Hitmarkers - RAID](https://modworkshop.net/mod/24560) improves the hitmarkers and and comes with different textures to switch between.
[Expanded communications wheel](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50106) Improves the communication wheel.
[Field Repairs](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59854) collection of small crash, stability and performance fixes, each one switchable.
[Grenade Quickthrow](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50294) Keybind to quickthrow grenades and other projectiles.
[HitlerSynced](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59855) synchronizes the random debriefing video for all players (host needs the mod).
[LoadoutProfiles](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59852) remembers your loadout (weapons, melee, grenade, skins) per skill profile.
[LootFixer](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50232) Removes unreachable loots, dogtags and greed caches from certain levels.
[Open profile in RAID files](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49000) Opens player's profile in the 'RAID Files' stats-webpage.
[Outlaw Intel Peeker Reborn](https://modworkshop.net/mod/48992) shows an icon on the intel notification for the found mission.
[PlayerInfo](https://modworkshop.net/mod/48990) shows the proficencies of other players.
[RandomMissionHotkey](https://modworkshop.net/mod/52639) Hotkey to start a random mission.
[Reload Then Run - RAID](https://modworkshop.net/mod/47652) prevents you from running, when weapon reload is almost done.
[ReadyUpLockFix](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59728) tries to fix the hard lock in the ready-up screen when players join or leave (host only).
[Simple Compass RAID:WW2](https://modworkshop.net/mod/48285) adds a configurable compass to the top of the screen.
[StatsScreen](https://modworkshop.net/mod/59625) a lifetime statistics screen in the Raid menu options.
[Slightly More Eye-Catching Enemies](https://modworkshop.net/mod/48945) Re-textures most of the common enemy types to be easier to tell apart.
[You have every card](https://modworkshop.net/mod/35694) Blatant cheat to always have every challenge card.
[RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760) Required by mods below (obviously).

##### BeardLib required to be auto updated, but works without it:
[Coloured Loading Screens: RAID Edition](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50094) Replaces the blue-grey colourless images on the loading screen with coloured variants.
[No Special Edition skin on Kübelwagen car](https://modworkshop.net/mod/43154) reverts the special edition car to normal (gold rush etc).

##### BeardLib required:
[No dumb percentages](https://modworkshop.net/mod/35759) always shows objectives in countable numbers.
[Pickpocket mission equipment](https://modworkshop.net/mod/50041) Allows you to steal mission equipment by pickpocketing enemies who have it.

mod.name: RAID-SuperBLT
mod.desc:
# RAID-SuperBLT

Mod loader for RAID: World War II. It lets the game load Lua mods and asset overlays, and is the foundation most RAID mods build on.
RAID-SuperBLT is a port of [SuperBLT](https://superblt.znix.xyz/) (PAYDAY 2) to RAID.

## Installation

1. Extract the `mods` directory and **one** DLL of your choice into your `steamapps/common/RAID World War II/` directory (overwrite when asked).
   - `WSOCK32.dll` (preferred)
   - `IPHLPAPI.dll` (alternative, in case WSOCK32 doesn't work for you)
   - Use only one of them. If both are present, `IPHLPAPI.dll` takes over and `WSOCK32.dll` deactivates itself.
2. Optional, but most mods need it: install [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760).

### Linux / Proton
Add this to your Steam launch options:
`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="WSOCK32,IPHLPAPI=n,b" %command%`

## Updating from RaidBLT

RaidBLT and RAID-SuperBLT conflict, so remove RaidBLT first:
1. Delete `IPHLPAPI.dll` (RaidBLT's one is **not** the same file as RAID-SuperBLT's one, even if you keep that file name).
2. Delete `mods/base/`.

Keep `saves`, `downloads`, `logs` and all your other mods. Then install as described above.
## Mod compatibility

- **Mods with a `supermod.xml`** load natively.
- **Old RaidBLT mods** (only a `mod.xml`) are loaded through [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760), so BeardLib is needed for these.
- **BeardLib mods** (`main.xml`) work as usual.

## Features

- Lua hook framework with a proper mod manager, options and keybinds menus (the mod options list scrolls when you have many mods)
- Asset database and asset overlays
- Wren scripting: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/wren/core_sblt_api/
- Automatic mod updates via ModWorkshop or custom update servers: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/updates/
- Mod dependencies: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/dependencies/
- Modern HTTPS for `dohttpreq()`: current libcurl (Schannel, HTTP/2, IPv6, HSTS, gzip), now also with methods, headers, request bodies and cookies
- Works together with BeardLib

## For mod developers

Developer documentation: https://superblt.znix.xyz/ (everything about XAudio doesn't apply to RAID).

**Porting an existing mod:** usually a `supermod.xml` next to your existing files is enough. Note that RAID uses `supermod.xml`, not PAYDAY 2's `mod.txt`. For examples, see my mods: https://modworkshop.net/user/bangl?game=543&category=567
The old RaidBLT XML modules for options and menus were not ported. Use the BeardLib ones (where they originally come from) or write them yourself.

**RaidBLT and BeardLib notes:**
- Without BeardLib: you can ship `mod.xml` and `supermod.xml` side by side. BeardLib ignores `mod.xml` when a `supermod.xml` exists, so the mod isn't loaded twice.
- With BeardLib: `mod.xml` (RaidBLT), `supermod.xml` (SuperBLT) and `main.xml` (BeardLib) can all be present.

## Source

DLL: https://github.com/RAIDModding/RAID-SuperBLT
Lua (base): https://github.com/RAIDModding/RAID-SuperBLT-Lua
Thumbnail image by Dribbleondo

detail.name: BangHUD-RAID
detail.desc:
This HUD addition lets you focus on your health, stamina, warcry and revives left by showing it in the screen's center (in addition to the vanilla HUD), where your eyes are much more likely to keep track of them.

To not actually block your vision, there are several options like transparency and exact positioning.

Should be compatible with pretty much any other HUD mod out there, since it's an extra panel layer and does not replace or depend on vanilla HUD panels.
However, 1.2 added options to hide those.

## Installation

1. Extract the `mods` directory and **one** DLL of your choice into your `steamapps/common/RAID World War II/` directory (overwrite when asked).
   - `WSOCK32.dll` (preferred)
   - `IPHLPAPI.dll` (alternative, in case WSOCK32 doesn't work for you)
   - Use only one of them. If both are present, `IPHLPAPI.dll` takes over and `WSOCK32.dll` deactivates itself.
2. Optional, but most mods need it: install [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760).

### Linux / Proton
Add this to your Steam launch options:
`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="WSOCK32,IPHLPAPI=n,b" %command%`

RaidBLT and RAID-SuperBLT conflict, so remove RaidBLT first:
1. Delete `IPHLPAPI.dll` (RaidBLT's one is **not** the same file as RAID-SuperBLT's one, even if you keep that file name).
2. Delete `mods/base/`.

Keep `saves`, `downloads`, `logs` and all your other mods. Then install as described above.
## Mod compatibility

- **Mods with a `supermod.xml`** load natively.
- **Old RaidBLT mods** (only a `mod.xml`) are loaded through [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760), so BeardLib is needed for these.
- **BeardLib mods** (`main.xml`) work as usual.

- Lua hook framework with a proper mod manager, options and keybinds menus (the mod options list scrolls when you have many mods)

- Mod dependencies: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/dependencies/
- Modern HTTPS for `dohttpreq()`: current libcurl (Schannel, HTTP/2, IPv6, HSTS, gzip), now also with methods, headers, request bodies and cookies

detail.desc:
# RAIDWW2-BeardLib

A library for RAID: World War II mods. It's the base for custom maps and many other mods.

## Features
- **Custom raids and operations:** add your own missions to the game. They show up in the camp like vanilla raids, with intel, loot, stealth, loading screens and more. Includes outlaw raids and operations (chains of raids).
- **Multiplayer:** players without the map download it automatically when the host picks it, or when they join a running game. Vanilla players are turned away with a clear message.
- **Map updater:** installed maps are updated in place.
- **Script file manipulation:** replace and extend game files (XML, Lua tweak data, ...) without overriding other mods.
- **Modules framework:** define your mod in XML (`main.xml`), including assets, localization, keybinds and custom achievements.
- **RaidBLT compatibility:** loads old RaidBLT mods (with only a `mod.xml`) so they keep working under RAID-SuperBLT.

## Making maps
Use the [BeardLib-Editor](https://github.com/diesel-modding/RAID-BeardLib-Editor). The documentation of custom raids and operations is in its README.
*(still in development / beta.)*

## Documentation for mod developers
There is no RAID specific documentation yet. Much of the PAYDAY 2 documentation still applies: [wiki](https://luffyyy.gitbook.io/beardlib)
Keep in mind that many PAYDAY 2 specific modules were removed (narratives and heists, for example), only the basics apply. Audio modding is not implemented yet in RAID. Templates are PAYDAY 2 only for now: https://github.com/ModWorkshop/BeardLib-Templates

# 5.1.0.4
- Fixed: The custom achievement list is now rebuilt every time the achievement menu is
  opened.

# 5.1.0.3
- Fixed: Custom achievement rewards (gold/XP) could get lost. They were only
  added in memory and the profile was not saved, so a failed mission or leaving
  the game as a client before the next regular save discarded the reward even
  though the achievement was marked as completed. The profile is now saved
  right after a reward is granted.

# 5.1.0.2:
- levels without nav data no longer crash the game when the player spawns: GroupAIStateBase:get_area_from_nav_seg_id hands out an empty area instead of nil (levels with nav data keep vanilla behaviour)
- mod loading order: the priority sort handles mods without a (numeric) priority and no longer mixes up valid and invalid configs
- ModCore:Config() returned the opposite of what it says (not self._config)
- function hooks: the hook tables may be missing, overrides are removed back to front while iterating, pre hooks are removed under their own name instead of removing hooks of the same function by other mods
- safe callbacks pass their arguments on to the function, and the error message shows what was thrown when it is not a table with a code
- Table:merge style helpers: no error when the parent table is missing; the type check of a nil value is correct when nil is allowed
- package manager: dynamic loading in the menu was inverted (dyn_load_menu loaded outside the menu), removed the leftover debug logging of the package loading
- file manager: the error for an unknown process mode printed the wrong variable

# 5.1.0.1

- Fix: Mission executions that the host sent before an instance existed on the client were never run on the client, because the queue was not processed after the instance point. For example, in the castle raid the dynamite bag of the drop pod was not hidden, so clients could pick it up before opening the pod.
- MenuUI: skip items with a dead panel when aligning

# 5.1.0.0

Custom raids and operations: BeardLib maps now work on RAID's actual mission structure (jobs and levels streamed into the camp level) instead of PAYDAY 2's narratives.

## Custom raids and operations
- **Custom raids (`<job>`):** A job is one mission with one level. The level is streamed into the camp like a vanilla raid, loaded when its world is prepared and unloaded when the raid ends. Custom raids are always unlocked and need no progression.
- **Job features:** icons per place, intel photos, loading screen, loot (dogtags and greed items), stealth, audio briefing, excluded continents, bounty filters.
- **Custom operations (`<operation>`):** A chain of events, each event is a job of the same project. Events in the same row are alternatives. Operations have their own icons, photos and strings, and free play is on by default.
- **Custom outlaw raids:** A job with `consumable="true"` is unlocked by outlaw intel and used up when played. Custom ones are left out while someone in the lobby couldn't play them (no BeardLib or no map).
- **Map updater:** Installed maps are updated in place and reloaded without a restart, the game only restarts if the engine holds changed files. The map files are unloaded when its raid ends.
- Documentation for jobs and operations is in the BeardLib-Editor README.

## Multiplayer
- BeardLib announces itself and its custom jobs in the join request. Vanilla clients are turned away by the host (with a proper message, as RAID has no text for that case).
- A BeardLib client without the map downloads it when the host selects it, or before joining a running job. The host waits for the download and is told if a peer declined.
- The map version is sent with the job info, and the client is offered the update on a mismatch.
- Custom operations show up as raids in the lobby, the server browser no longer crashes on operations the browsing client doesn't have.
- Lobbies of custom jobs the client doesn't have are listed.

## Profile guard
Whatever the game stores under the id of a custom job or level (statistics, progression, breadcrumbs, save slots of custom operations) is removed from the saved profile, so uninstalling a map leaves no leftovers. Only the written copy is cleaned, the running game is left alone. Option "Profile guard", on by default.

## Fixes
- Fixed an endless recursion (crash) when a level is started a second time.
- Script replacements of a streamed level were registered on every start and piled up, now once.
- An operation with the same job in more than one event crashed when started, such a job is now ignored.
- Pasting text into text boxes checked the pressed key instead of the clipboard for forbidden characters.
- A job that is used by multiple events of an operation no longer crashes the game.
- Fixed `start_in_stealth` and `stealth_description` contradicting each other.
- ImageButton: support for rotation and `wrap_mode`.
- Backported fixes from the PAYDAY 2 BeardLib.

## For map authors
- **Narratives are replaced by jobs.** Old `<narrative>` maps report how to migrate. A job is one mission with one level, there are no chains.
- Removed: the `bounty_forbid_buffs` attribute (the daily bounty uses a fixed list of vanilla jobs) and the dead `AIGroupType` element.
- Maps need an `<AssetUpdates id="<MWS-ID>" provider="modworkshop"/>` in their `main.xml` so clients can download them.

detail.name: Bots Have Feelings - Reborn
detail.desc:
Improvements for your team-mate bots. Everything works for unmodded clients as well, but clients that have the mod too get the shout functions and UI elements (carry amounts, icons).

Requires [RAID-SuperBLT](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49744) (base 2.4.0 or newer). Updates come directly from the mod's git repository (automatic via SuperBLT).

## Carrying
- The carry system for bots is entirely rewritten, including stacking and netcode.
- Bots catch thrown bags and carry them along the routes players throw them (Monkeepers mode). Corpses, ladders, parachutes, turrets, flak shell pallets and tank shells are not caught.
- Bots carry loot into a nearby secure zone (truck, boat, ...) and throw it in (host only), and drop what they still carry at the mission end.
- Bots are slowed down while carrying (option).
- Bots keep their bag for short jobs (flare, flee, pickup, revive).

## Commands and modes
- Shout commands listen for spoken sounds, so they also work with the comm wheels of unmodded clients.
- Two wait modes when loud: stationary (holds the spot) and use cover (takes cover near the spot and returns once healthy). The comm wheel "wait" and the quick shout toggle cycle through them.
- Follow / wait in stealth, defend_area mode (call wait).
- Icons on the teammate panel and name label: follow target, wait mode, revive job (white = somebody else, red = you), carry job.

## Combat
- Bots prioritize enemies marked by players (option).
- Bots avoid live grenades and fires, and return to what they were doing.
- Optional bot grenades: bots only throw at groups and never when someone would be inside the blast radius. The throwable is selectable per bot.
- Bot weapons: MP38, StG44, Thompson, Garand, Geco and Kar98k as primary.
- "No unnecessary revives": bots do not revive someone who is already being revived.
- Respawn timer of dead bots next to their name.
- Experimental: bots stay detectable in stealth but back off when a guard looks their way (bots_avoid_guards), and sneak up on lone guards to take them out with a melee strike (bots_melee_guards).
- Bots put out spotter flares.

## Usage tips
- Shouting (default F) while holding shift makes a bot drop all his bags.
- Options are in the SuperBLT mod options menu.

Full compat to 'competent bots': when it's installed, it gets higher prio for offline mode and still applies its reduced falloff damage (so increased overall bot damage).

Originally based on this awesome mod: https://modworkshop.net/mod/30435

mod.desc:
# RAID-SuperBLT

Mod loader for RAID: World War II. It lets the game load Lua mods and asset overlays, and is the foundation most RAID mods build on.
RAID-SuperBLT is a port of [SuperBLT](https://superblt.znix.xyz/) (PAYDAY 2) to RAID.

## Installation

1. Extract the `mods` directory and **one** DLL of your choice into your `steamapps/common/RAID World War II/` directory (overwrite when asked).
   - `WSOCK32.dll` (preferred)
   - `IPHLPAPI.dll` (alternative, in case WSOCK32 doesn't work for you)
   - Use only one of them. If both are present, `IPHLPAPI.dll` takes over and `WSOCK32.dll` deactivates itself.
2. Optional, but most mods need it: install [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760).

### Linux / Proton
Add this to your Steam launch options:
`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="WSOCK32,IPHLPAPI=n,b" %command%`

## Updating from RaidBLT

RaidBLT and RAID-SuperBLT conflict, so remove RaidBLT first:
1. Delete `IPHLPAPI.dll` (RaidBLT's one is **not** the same file as RAID-SuperBLT's one, even if you keep that file name).
2. Delete `mods/base/`.

Keep `saves`, `downloads`, `logs` and all your other mods. Then install as described above.
## Mod compatibility

- **Mods with a `supermod.xml`** load natively.
- **Old RaidBLT mods** (only a `mod.xml`) are loaded through [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760), so BeardLib is needed for these.
- **BeardLib mods** (`main.xml`) work as usual.

## Features

- Lua hook framework with a proper mod manager, options and keybinds menus (the mod options list scrolls when you have many mods)
- Asset database and asset overlays
- Wren scripting: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/wren/core_sblt_api/
- Automatic mod updates via ModWorkshop or custom update servers: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/updates/
- Mod dependencies: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/dependencies/
- Modern HTTPS for `dohttpreq()`: current libcurl (Schannel, HTTP/2, IPv6, HSTS, gzip), now also with methods, headers, request bodies and cookies
- Works together with BeardLib

## For mod developers

Developer documentation: https://superblt.znix.xyz/ (everything about XAudio doesn't apply to RAID).

**Porting an existing mod:** usually a `supermod.xml` next to your existing files is enough. Note that RAID uses `supermod.xml`, not PAYDAY 2's `mod.txt`. For examples, see my mods: https://modworkshop.net/user/bangl?game=543&category=567
The old RaidBLT XML modules for options and menus were not ported. Use the BeardLib ones (where they originally come from) or write them yourself.

**RaidBLT and BeardLib notes:**
- Without BeardLib: you can ship `mod.xml` and `supermod.xml` side by side. BeardLib ignores `mod.xml` when a `supermod.xml` exists, so the mod isn't loaded twice.
- With BeardLib: `mod.xml` (RaidBLT), `supermod.xml` (SuperBLT) and `main.xml` (BeardLib) can all be present.

## Source

Removes unreachable loots, dogtags and greed caches from:
- enigmatic (in the vault)
- rolling stock (behind the fences and on the bridge)

detail.name: ReadyUpLockFix
detail.desc:
Tries to fix the hard lock in the ready-up screen when players join or leave while it is open.

Note: this is an attempt. It is not proven that it fixes the lock. The cause was worked out from the game's code and the mod covers the paths that look responsible, but the lock is hard to reproduce, so it is untested whether it really prevents it.

Problem: the ready-up screen builds its player list once, when it opens. The host re-opens the lobby at the same moment, so someone can join into a screen that cannot represent them. They never get a challenge card entry, "everyone ready" can never become true, and the raid never starts. Players leaving at the wrong moment can also break the screen.

What the mod does:
- Keeps the lobby closed for as long as the ready-up screen is open (host)
- Makes the screen robust against players who left or joined late (no more nil errors, left/kicked players stay shown but no longer block the ready check)
- Ignores unknown late joiners when checking whether everyone has locked a card

Install it on the host; clients do not need it. No options, nothing to configure.

If you still end up with a locked lobby while using this, please upload your log to pastebin.com or similar and send me the link. I will look into it.

detail.name: AssaultInfoRAID
detail.desc:
Shows what the assault AI is doing, in a small info box on your HUD.

The box shows the current phase and updates live:
- Phase: Stealth, Assault Incoming, Build, Sustain, Fade, Regroup, Next Assault, Hunt Mode (the title flashes and changes color on each phase change)
- Time left until the assault ends (for build and sustain phases, the whole remaining assault is estimated)
- Enemies alive vs. the current target force
- Kills left until the assault falls back to fade

It is hidden in the camp.

Hosting vs. joining:
- As host you get the full information.
- As client you get the full information too, if the host runs this mod. The host sends its data to every client that has it (nothing else is changed in the netcode, other players are not affected).
- Without the mod on the host, you get a reduced box: the phase only (assault, hunt, stealth), no times or counts.

detail.desc:
# Field Repairs

Collection of small crash, stability and performance fixes for RAID: WW2. Each fix is one hook
and one file in `lua/`; they are independent of each other. Each can be switched off in Options > Field Repairs
(saved in `saves/FieldRepairs.json`, applies at once; the callback queue from the next raid).

Author: BangL

| Fix | Hook | File | Problem |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Husk customization crash](#husk-customization-crash) | `lib/units/characters/charactercustomization` | `lua/CharacterCustomization.lua` | Engine crash when a joiner aborts while the husk is spawned |
| [Mission script callback queue](#mission-script-callback-queue) | `lib/managers/missionmanager` | `lua/MissionScript.lua` | Frametime spikes in maps with many polling mission elements (Odin's Fall) |
| [Mission world leak](#mission-world-leak) | `core/lib/managers/coreworldcollection` | `lua/CoreWorldCollection.lua` | 10-20 MB of Lua heap stay behind per raid that is started and left |
| [Waypoint without target](#waypoint-without-target) | `lib/managers/hudmanager` | `lua/HUDManager.lua` | Lua error when a waypoint has neither position nor unit |
| [Portal group unit leak](#portal-group-unit-leak) | `core/lib/managers/coreportalmanager` | `lua/CorePortalManager.lua` | Removed units stay referenced in portal unit groups |
| [Corpses in enemy detection](#corpses-in-enemy-detection) | `lib/managers/group_ai_states/groupaistatebase` | `lua/GroupAIStateBase.lua` | Detection walks every corpse per unit and tick, bad frametime in big fights with a high corpse limit |
| [Bot weapon when downed](#bot-weapon-when-downed) | `lib/units/player_team/teamaiinventory`, `huskteamaiinventory` | `lua/TeamAIInventory.lua` | A downed bot shoots with its weapon hidden |
| [Turret gunner damage](#turret-gunner-damage) | `lib/units/weapons/turretweapon` | `lua/TurretWeapon.lua` | Possible engine crash from explosion damage with a destroyed attacker unit |

## Bot walk action after mission restart

`CopActionWalk:update` can run for a husk bot (`HuskTeamAIMovement:_upd_actions`) after the host restarted the mission and the
unit was torn down on the client. An extension (`_ext_base`/`_ext_anim`) is nil, the Lua error reaches the engine update uncaught
and the game dies with a C++ exception.

The hook skips the update if the unit is gone or an extension is missing, and wraps the rest in `blt.pcall` (errors are logged).

### Risks

- Cause is a hypothesis from the Lua stack (client crash during a host mission restart), not reproduced.
- The `blt.pcall` swallows any other error in the walk update too, so a bug there shows only as a log line and a stuck unit.

## Installation

copy the `Field Repairs` folder to `mods/`. Requires SuperBLT 2.x (`blt.pcall`, `BLT:Log`).

## Husk customization crash

`CharacterCustomization:_part_loaded_callback` is replaced by the vanilla function with alive
checks. The dyn_resource callback can fire synchronously while a husk is being spawned
(drop-in). If the husk is destroyed meanwhile (the joiner aborts), the native `get_object`,
`position` and `rotation` calls on dead objects crash the engine.

Differences to vanilla: the husk, the spawned part and both units of the bone loop are checked
with `alive()`; a part that could not be spawned is logged (`[Field Repairs] CharacterCustomization`)
and skipped; bones missing on either unit are skipped instead of erroring.

Risk: the whole function is replaced. A game patch that changes the original is overridden
silently.

## Mission script callback queue

Makes the callback queue of the mission scripts cheap. Fixes the recurring frametime spikes in
**Odin's Fall** (`flakturm`); every other map benefits in proportion to how many timed
mission elements it has.

### Symptom

Frametime spikes in Odin's Fall, about every 250 ms on the reporter's machine. They show up in
stealth too, even with nearly all enemies dead, and they get worse after other maps were played
first on a high difficulty. Other maps are not affected.

### Measurements

Everything was measured in the running game with LuaDebugAPI, difficulty 4, god mode on. The
"after 13 raids" runs follow a full cycle of all raids (`forest_gumpy` to `forest_bunker`).

| Map / state                              | median  | p95     | p99     | spike frames per 30 s |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| Camp                                     | 5.6 ms  | 6.0 ms  | 6.7 ms  | 4                     |
| Silo                                     | 5.6 ms  | 7.9 ms  | 8.7 ms  | 5                     |
| Odin's Fall, after 13 raids, **without** | 9-15 ms | 43 ms   | 68 ms   | 289                   |
| Odin's Fall, after 13 raids, **with**    | 10.6 ms | 11.6 ms | 12.5 ms | 7                     |

A spike frame is a frame gap of more than twice the median. Without the fix the spikes arrive
in a 0.1 s grid (30-45 ms) with larger ones every second (up to 75 ms). With it, only one engine
hitch remains (see "Remaining").

### Cause

- `GameSetup:update` spent on average 33 ms per spike frame in **Lua**, so it is not the
  renderer. Neither the number of enemies, the garbage collector (stopping it changed
  nothing), any single mission element (each takes 3 ms or less), nor any mod is responsible.
- The time is inside `CoreMissionManager.MissionScript:update`, in `CallbackHandler:update`
  (`core/lib/utils/coreevent.lua`). It keeps all timed callbacks in one ascending array and
  pays `table.remove(t, 1)` plus a sorted `table.insert(t, i, cb)` for **every** callback it
  runs.
- In this LuaJIT build `table.remove` is a Lua builtin. Moving one element costs about 1 us,
  and any other Lua operation costs about the same: 2M additions take 1.9 s. Native
  `table.insert` is fast, `table.remove(t, 1)` is not (169 elements: 160 us per call).
- Odin's Fall has about 170 queued callbacks in its `default` script. Almost all are
  `ElementAreaTrigger:update_area` and `update_lookat` polls with 0.1, 0.2 and 1.0 s
  intervals. 64 to 106 of them run per tick, and about 150 once per second. The array work
  is quadratic, which gives 20-35 ms per 0.1 s tick and about 70 ms per second.
- Silo and the camp have far fewer queued callbacks and never reach this.
- Why it gets worse after many other maps is **not** explained. Fresh-start Odin's Fall,
  without prior raids, measured clean.

### Fix

`lua/MissionScript.lua` replaces `__insert_sorted` and `update` on
`CoreMissionManager.MissionScript` (the instances use the core class, not the global
`MissionScript` subclass from `lib/managers/missionmanager`).

The 169 callbacks have only 7 distinct due times. Callbacks with the same due time now share
a bucket. Only the due times are kept in a descending array, so the next one is at the end
and popping it shifts nothing. Inserting a callback is a table lookup and an append. Buckets
and array live in `self._sorted`, so `clear()` resets both.

Semantics stay the same:

- Due callbacks run in ascending due time. On equal due time the newest runs first, as in the
  original, where a new entry was inserted in front of equal ones. A bucket is walked from the
  end.
- `times`, `interval` and re-queueing (`next + interval`) are copied unchanged.
- A callback that adds a new one while running gets it executed in the same update when it is
  already due, as before.
- `remove()` only clears `cb.next`. The entry stays queued and is skipped when its turn comes.
- The `_updators` loop is kept.
- Nothing else in the game or the installed mods reads `_sorted`.

### Verification

- **Differential test.** The same random scenarios (equal and different intervals, `times` of
  -1 to 3, removal of other callbacks and of itself, adding callbacks while running, varying
  frame times) ran through the original `CoreEvent.CallbackHandler` and through the patched
  `MissionScript`. 40 seeds and about 7000 executed callbacks gave 0 differences in order or
  time.
- **In game.** Full cycle of 13 raids with the fix loaded through its hook, then Odin's Fall.
  The queues stay consistent (33 and 168 entries, one expired one-shot callback), time advances
  and the log has no errors from the fix.
- **Not tested:** multiplayer, a complete raid with all scripted events (timers, waves,
  delays), and any before/after comparison on maps other than Odin's Fall.

### Remaining

- One hitch of 35-45 ms every ~4.5 s in Odin's Fall. Lua accounts for only 1-2 ms of it, the
  GC is not the cause, and a similar hitch (every 6-7 s) exists in Silo and the camp. It is an
  engine-side hitch, not specific to Odin's Fall.
- The median in Odin's Fall stays at about 10 ms (Silo: 5.6 ms), probably rendering of the
  level.

### Risks

- Buckets need exactly equal float due times. If they differ, there are just more buckets:
  still correct, only slower.
- A removed callback stays in its bucket until its due time (the original dropped it at the
  next update). Many removed callbacks with long intervals therefore stay in memory longer.
- Writes to `cb.next` of a queued callback from outside the queue are not supported and were
  not exhaustively searched for.
- The whole core `update` is replaced. A game patch to the original, or another mod that
  overrides `MissionScript:update` or `__insert_sorted`, would conflict.

## Mission world leak

Every raid that is started and left without a Lua reload leaves 10 to 20 MB behind in the Lua
heap. `CoreWorldCollection:destroy_world` is wrapped and lets go of what belongs to the
destroyed world, and nothing else:

- **Nav links.** `NavigationManager:unregister_anim_nav_link` removes a link from the engine,
  but the engine keeps its user data table `{element = element}` in the registry, which holds
  the whole mission script. The world never calls `ElementNavLink:destroy`, so the links are
  unregistered here and `element` is cleared in the registry tables.
- **Callbacks of destroyed elements.** `MissionManager._runned_unit_sequences_callbacks` and the
  `_use_unit_callbacks` of the main world definition are only emptied when the whole simulation
  stops. Callbacks of the elements of the destroyed world are removed from them. A callback
  belongs to an element if its first upvalue is that element (callbacks made with
  `callback(object, ...)`).

Failures while collecting or releasing are caught with `blt.pcall` and logged as warnings
(`[Field Repairs] Could not ...`); the original `destroy_world` always runs.

Risks: the registry is scanned once per destroyed world. The upvalue check only finds
callbacks that follow the `callback(object, ...)` pattern; others stay (no wrong removal,
just no gain).

## Waypoint without target

`HUDManager:add_waypoint` does `data.position or data.unit:position()`. If a waypoint has no
position and its unit is nil or dead, that errors. The wrapper skips such a waypoint and logs a
warning (`[Field Repairs] Waypoint <id> has neither position nor unit`). Idea from The Fixes (PD2).

## Portal group unit leak

`PortalUnitGroup:remove_unit_id` only clears the id, the unit stays in `_units`. The wrapper
also removes that unit (by identity) from `_units`. Idea from Celer (PD2).

## Corpses in enemy detection

### Symptom

Big fights (20+ enemies) get slow, 16 FPS in Settlement with the corpse limit (video settings) at 128.

### Measurements

Live with `LuaDebugAPI`, 10 s window, 26 living enemies, 129 corpses:

- `EnemyManager:update` 74% of the frame time, nearly all of it `CopLogicBase._upd_attention_obj_detection`
  (68%, about 3 ms per call, ~210 calls per second).
- Each call walks ~159 attention objects: 129 corpses (slot 17), 26 living enemies, bots and players.
  About 250,000 loop iterations per second, 80% of them for dead units.
- Mission area triggers, `GroupAIStateBase:update`, HUD and movement together stay below 10%.

### Cause

A dead enemy stays a registered attention object until its corpse is disposed of, which happens at
`corpse_limit` (default 32, up to 250). Every living enemy and bot checks every one of them each detection tick.

### Fix

`get_AI_attention_objects_by_filter` returns a copy without dead units once the level is loud. In stealth the vanilla set
is used, guards still find bodies. The copy is cached per filter and rebuilt when an attention object is registered,
changed or removed, and at the latest after a second (units that died since). The vanilla sets are not touched.

### Risks

- Enemies and bots do not react to corpses while loud. Nothing in the vanilla code uses that (only the stealth
  voice lines and alerts for bodies), but this was read from the code, not played through.
- A unit that died stays in the set for up to a second.

## Bot weapon when downed

A bot that goes down hides its weapon: the downed animation calls the hide_weapon callback of `CopInventory`, which ends in
`PlayerInventory:hide_equipped_unit`. The bot keeps shooting (with the pistol, `SLOT_1`) but nobody sees a weapon in its hands.

`hide_equipped_unit` does nothing for `TeamAIInventory` and `HuskTeamAIInventory`. Equipping and unequipping still show and
place the weapon as before.

### Risks

- Only the local display changes, nothing is synced. Whether the hiding was intended (e.g. against clipping with the downed
  pose) is unknown; with the Luger and the M1911 it looked fine.
- The weapon also stays visible in other states that call the hide callback for bots (not checked: revive, carry).

## Turret gunner damage

`TurretWeapon:on_puppet_damaged` calls `attacker_unit:movement()` and `send_to_peers_synched(..., attacker_unit)` without checking
the unit. `FlamerTank` stores `peer:unit()` of the last molotov sync and uses it as the attacker of the explosion. If that unit
was destroyed in between, the call is an engine access violation (seen on the host, stack ended in `on_puppet_damaged`).

The hook returns early if `damage_info.attacker_unit` is not `alive()`.

### Risks

- Cause is a hypothesis from the Lua stack (the native callstack has no symbols), not reproduced.
- Damage to the gunner from such an explosion does not dazed-deactivate the turret.

# RAID-SuperBLT

Mod loader for RAID: World War II. It lets the game load Lua mods and asset overlays, and is the foundation most RAID mods build on.
RAID-SuperBLT is a port of [SuperBLT](https://superblt.znix.xyz/) (PAYDAY 2) to RAID.

## Installation

1. Extract the `mods` directory and **one** DLL of your choice into your `steamapps/common/RAID World War II/` directory (overwrite when asked).
   - `WSOCK32.dll` (preferred)
   - `IPHLPAPI.dll` (alternative, in case WSOCK32 doesn't work for you)
   - Use only one of them. If both are present, `IPHLPAPI.dll` takes over and `WSOCK32.dll` deactivates itself.
2. Optional, but most mods need it: install [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760).

### Linux / Proton
Add this to your Steam launch options:
`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="WSOCK32,IPHLPAPI=n,b" %command%`

## Updating from RaidBLT

RaidBLT and RAID-SuperBLT conflict, so remove RaidBLT first:
1. Delete `IPHLPAPI.dll` (RaidBLT's one is **not** the same file as RAID-SuperBLT's one, even if you keep that file name).
2. Delete `mods/base/`.

Keep `saves`, `downloads`, `logs` and all your other mods. Then install as described above.
## Mod compatibility

- **Mods with a `supermod.xml`** load natively.

- Automatic mod updates via ModWorkshop or custom update servers: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/updates/

detail.name: Camp Fixes
detail.desc:
# Camp Fixes

Repairs camp logic that shipped unfinished or unwired.

## What it does

- **Toilet break:** the camp contains a finished but disabled special objective,
  `so_camp_idle_peeing`, next to the toilet. Camp NPCs now and then walk over, use the toilet and
  comment on it (`banter_goldtoilet`), then pick the next random camp idle.
- **Golden bomb banter:** `banter_goldbomb` (trigger `trigger_special_objective_025`) belongs on the
  same objective as `tso_bombers` but has an empty target list, and the "unlocked" sequence that
  would swap the two is never run. With the golden bomb (level 2) applied, `tso_bombers` is
  disabled and the gold bomb trigger enabled and pointed at the bombers objective. Follows the
  applied camp upgrade, also when it is changed in the camp.
- **Piano and skills banter:** `tso_upg_skills` also listens to the piano objective, whose own
  `tso_piano` trigger plays the piano banter. The piano is removed from the skills trigger.
- **Spy's chair:** `so_camp_sit_idle_get_up001` (`so_camp_small_table_sit`) moves a bot onto the chair
  the camp spy (`raid_npc_spy_static`) sits on, and nothing checks that the chair is free. The
  objective is not offered while the spy is there.

## The bug behind it

`ElementSpecialObjective:add_event_callback` registers every trigger of a special objective under
the same id, so only the last trigger per event survives. The toilet objective has two triggers
per event (the one that re-rolls the camp idles was lost, which left the NPC standing at the
toilet), so each trigger of the affected objectives is registered under its own id here. Counted
over all missions this affects five (objective, event) groups, so the bug is not fixed globally.

## Options

BLT options -> Camp Fixes: toilet break, golden bomb banter, keep bots off the spy's chair.

## Install

Copy the `CampFixes` folder to `mods/`.

# RAID-SuperBLT

Mod loader for RAID: World War II. It lets the game load Lua mods and asset overlays, and is the foundation most RAID mods build on.
RAID-SuperBLT is a port of [SuperBLT](https://superblt.znix.xyz/) (PAYDAY 2) to RAID.

## Installation

1. Extract the `mods` directory and **one** DLL of your choice into your `steamapps/common/RAID World War II/` directory (overwrite when asked).
   - `WSOCK32.dll` (preferred)
   - `IPHLPAPI.dll` (alternative, in case WSOCK32 doesn't work for you)
   - Use only one of them. If both are present, `IPHLPAPI.dll` takes over and `WSOCK32.dll` deactivates itself.
2. Optional, but most mods need it: install [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760).

### Linux / Proton
Add this to your Steam launch options:
`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="WSOCK32,IPHLPAPI=n,b" %command%`

## Updating from RaidBLT

RaidBLT and RAID-SuperBLT conflict, so remove RaidBLT first:
1. Delete `IPHLPAPI.dll` (RaidBLT's one is **not** the same file as RAID-SuperBLT's one, even if you keep that file name).
2. Delete `mods/base/`.

Keep `saves`, `downloads`, `logs` and all your other mods. Then install as described above.
## Mod compatibility

- **Mods with a `supermod.xml`** load natively.
- **Old RaidBLT mods** (only a `mod.xml`) are loaded through [RAIDWW2-BeardLib](https://modworkshop.net/mod/49760), so BeardLib is needed for these.
- **BeardLib mods** (`main.xml`) work as usual.

## Features

- Lua hook framework with a proper mod manager, options and keybinds menus (the mod options list scrolls when you have many mods)
- Asset database and asset overlays
- Wren scripting: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/wren/core_sblt_api/
- Automatic mod updates via ModWorkshop or custom update servers: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/updates/
- Mod dependencies: https://superblt.znix.xyz/doc/mod_definition/dependencies/
- Modern HTTPS for `dohttpreq()`: current libcurl (Schannel, HTTP/2, IPv6, HSTS, gzip), now also with methods, headers, request bodies and cookies
- Works together with BeardLib

## For mod developers

Developer documentation: https://superblt.znix.xyz/ (everything about XAudio doesn't apply to RAID).

**Porting an existing mod:** usually a `supermod.xml` next to your existing files is enough. Note that RAID uses `supermod.xml`, not PAYDAY 2's `mod.txt`. For examples, see my mods: https://modworkshop.net/user/bangl?game=543&category=567
The old RaidBLT XML modules for options and menus were not ported. Use the BeardLib ones (where they originally come from) or write them yourself.

**RaidBLT and BeardLib notes:**
- Without BeardLib: you can ship `mod.xml` and `supermod.xml` side by side. BeardLib ignores `mod.xml` when a `supermod.xml` exists, so the mod isn't loaded twice.
- With BeardLib: `mod.xml` (RaidBLT), `supermod.xml` (SuperBLT) and `main.xml` (BeardLib) can all be present.
